A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FoundationStereo. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, qualitative predictions, architecture ablations, and a supplementary self-curation experiment.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds FSD transfer experiments, Booster evaluation, resolution and resource measurements, and a Middlebury leaderboard result.

M1.justification: The STA backbone, APC and disparity-transformer filtering, GRU refinement, training loss, and iterative self-curation procedure remain unchanged. The added explanation of latent monocular features clarifies the existing architecture.

E1.justification: v3 newly evaluates Booster, covering specular and transparent objects; v1 only discusses it as related work. Existing training datasets and benchmark coverage remain. Spring and UnrealStereo4K are added to descriptive Table 1, without evidence that they were used for training or evaluation.

E2.justification: The new Middlebury leaderboard comparison in Figure 8 includes AIO-Stereo, DEFOM-Stereo, and RSM, absent from v1's Middlebury comparisons. Existing main-table comparator sets are retained, while the other new appendix experiments reuse previously included methods.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce FSD-only baseline training and full-, half-, and quarter-resolution Middlebury evaluation with runtime and peak-memory measurements on a common 3090 GPU. Full-resolution FoundationStereo uses maximum disparity 320. The original optimization schedule and metric definitions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 9 adds controlled Scene Flow-versus-FSD training comparisons for IGEV and Selective-IGEV, testing whether the dataset benefits other architectures. Table 10 adds resolution sensitivity and accuracy-resource analysis. These substantially extend validation beyond v1's architecture, dataset-inclusion, and self-curation ablations, which are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. The added dataset-averaged runtime measurements do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises the full-model scores from 1.2/1.4/1.9/2.2 to 1.1/0.5/2.3/2.8 and RAFT-Stereo's Middlebury score from 9.4 to 12.6. Table 3 changes FoundationStereo's EPE from 0.33 to 0.34. Substantial new results cover FSD transfer, Booster, resolution/resource comparisons, and first place on the Middlebury leaderboard. The PDFs do not establish the cause of the numerical revisions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, attention and GRU formulations, disparity prediction, and loss equations remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about zero-shot stereo generalization, the synthetic dataset, STA, and AHCF. The new leaderboard and appendix results add supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explains why latent monocular features are used instead of scale-ambiguous raw monocular depth. Section 10 adds discussion of desktop-GPU feasibility and resolution-dependent memory bottlenecks. The original efficiency and transparent-object limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies default maximum disparity 416 and Middlebury evaluation at half resolution on non-occluded regions, plus hardware and settings for the new resource comparison. These disclosures do not establish changes to retained experiments. The explicit promise to release code, model, and data is removed, while the project-page link remains.

R1.justification: v3 adds Correlate-and-Excite as attribution for hourglass filtering and adds Spring and SMD-Nets/UnrealStereo4K to the dataset comparison and references. These are limited additions; the overall research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained. Changes include a short architectural clarification, correction of SAD to FSD, supplementary section expansion and renumbering, and small conclusion and acknowledgement edits.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two dataset columns. The supplement adds Tables 9–10, a Booster table and qualitative panel, and the Middlebury leaderboard screenshot. The existing disparity histogram is resized and renumbered as Figure 9; the main figures and overall document design are retained.

improvement.justification: The new FSD transfer tests, difficult-material evaluation, and resolution/resource analysis strengthen validation and clarify practical costs. Added evaluation settings also improve reproducibility. The overall gain is limited by sparse documentation of Middlebury fine-tuning and a new inconsistency: Table 3 reports 0.34 EPE while Section 4.4 still states 0.33.
